methods.label: Chain the power equations
methods.explanation:
The result of each power is the base in the next equation. Raising successively to the next exponent therefore combines all four equations. Since every base is positive, the power-of-a-power law gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
4^{ab}&=(4^a)^b=5^b=6,\\
4^{abc}&=(4^{ab})^c=6^c=7,\\
4^{abcd}&=(4^{abc})^d=7^d=8.
\end{aligned}
\]
Now \(4=2^2\) and \(8=2^3\), so
\[
2^{2abcd}=2^3.
\]
Powers of \(2\) increase strictly with their exponents, so equal powers have equal exponents. Thus \(2abcd=3\), giving \(abcd=\frac32\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses positive-base power laws and the fact that equal powers of a base greater than 1 have equal exponents. No logarithms are used.
